findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at class-definition time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. Every instance created via `from_integration` (which never passes `queued`) will therefore carry the process start time rather than the actual time the assignment was queued. Since the field is named `queued` and is meant to record when the inbound change happened, its value will be wrong/stale (constant per process). Fix by using `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: Datetime in task kwargs is not JSON-serializable by Celery
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` includes the `queued` datetime field, and the resulting dict is passed directly as a Celery task kwarg in `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async`. Sentry's Celery defaults use the JSON serializer, which cannot encode `datetime` objects, so enqueueing the task will raise a `EncodeError` and the outbound sync will silently never run for any inbound-triggered assignment (the exact path this PR is meant to fix). The dict should serialize the datetime (e.g. `isoformat()`), and `from_dict` should parse it back.

findings.title: Inbound sync ignores `organization_id` scope when assigning
findings.body: `sync_group_assignee_inbound` calls `where_should_sync(integration, "inbound_assignee")` without the optional `organization_id`, and `where_should_sync` itself never threads the assignment source through to `should_sync` (line 48 calls it with one argument). Any future/other caller relying on `where_should_sync` to respect the source integration will not get cycle protection; more importantly the `should_sync` signature change means the inbound/outbound gating in `where_should_sync` cannot participate in the new cycle-prevention mechanism at all, so the fix only covers the direct `sync_assignee_outbound` task path. If status sync or other `should_sync` callers were intended to be covered (the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature was changed to accept `assignment_source`), that wiring is missing.

findings.title: No test that a different integration still receives the outbound sync
findings.body: The new test only covers the case where the assignment source matches the target integration (asserting `assert_not_called`). The stated design intent — "This should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward" — is not tested anywhere. A regression that suppresses all outbound assignee syncs whenever any assignment source is present would pass the current test suite. Add a test with two integrations linked to the group where the source is integration A and assert integration B's `sync_assignee_outbound` is still called.

findings.title: `from_dict` accepts unvalidated/extra fields silently or returns None on type mismatch
findings.body: `cls(**input_dict)` will happily construct an `AssignmentSource` with `integration_id` set to a string or arbitrary values without validation, and any extra key causes a `TypeError` swallowed into `None`, which then disables cycle protection entirely (parsed source becomes None and the outbound sync proceeds). Because this dict crosses a Celery boundary from potentially old/new producer versions, a mismatched payload silently reverts to the looping behavior the PR is fixing rather than surfacing an error. Consider logging when parsing fails and validating types.
